newsitem.title: CHINA: China details move to pull bank funds from bourse.
newsitem.headline: China details move to pull bank funds from bourse.

text.p: China gave new details of its plans to halt the flow of bank funds into the stock market, setting a deadline for commercial banks to unwind positions on the bourse.
State television also said commercial banks must stop trading of treasury debt repurchase agreements on the nation's two stock exchanges, effective Friday.
These were part of previously announced measures aimed at limiting financial risk to protect the banking system which has pumped huge amounts of cash into the buoyant stock markets.
State television said that commercial banks must unwind positions in the stock market within 10 days of receipt of formal notice of the rules.
All commercial bank repurchase trades must be switched to the off-exchange interbank market.
The central bank has been concerned that the repurchase market had been a key part of the funding of stock speculation which had pumped up the domestic indices 50 percent earlier this year.
It is also hoping to expand the interbank market to help it manage money supply more efficiently.
The television report repeated a ban on overdrafts used for buying stocks, and said that each commercial bank had to investigate its own activities to ensure they complied with the regulations.
Securities companies and other financial institutions found manipulating the stock market could be dealt with under criminal law, the television report warned. it gave no further details.
